buttonLabel: "Explore tours of Colombia"
lead: >-
  Choose a tour of Colombia based on how much time you want to spend in its cities, coffee-growing region, natural areas, and on the Caribbean coast. In 5–7 days, you can visit several major cities, while longer itineraries add plantations, islands, or dedicated trips to Caño Cristales. Compare Ada Tours itineraries by their actual daily schedules, transfers, and included services.
---

## Tours of Colombia: how to choose the right itinerary

**Start by deciding what you want from the journey.** For a first visit, routes through [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/), [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/), and [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/) are a good fit. Coffee lovers should allow a separate day at a working farm, while anyone hoping to see [Caño Cristales](/colombia/place/cano-cristales/) needs to factor in the season and the logistics of visiting this natural area.

We offer {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. Trips of the same duration do not necessarily offer the same experiences: one may combine 2–3 cities and domestic flights, another may focus on longer nature excursions, and a third may include an island stay. The best starting point for comparison is the day-by-day itinerary.

| Tour | Main distinguishing feature |
|---|---|
| [Bogotá and Cartagena, 5 days](/colombia/tour/colombia-essential-5-days/) | The capital, Guatavita, Zipaquirá, and the Rosario Islands |
| [Three cities, 7 days](/colombia/tour/colombia-highlights-7-days/) | Bogotá, Medellín, Guatapé, and Cartagena |
| [Caño Cristales, 8 days](/colombia/tour/colombia-cano-cristales-8-days/) | La Macarena and dedicated nature excursions |
| [Cities and coffee, 10 days](/colombia/tour/colombia-bogota-medellin-cartagena-coffee-10-days/) | Cultural experiences and a coffee farm |
| [Many Faces of Colombia, 11 days](/colombia/tour/colombia-complete-11-days/) | The coffee region, San Andrés Island, and Medellín |
| [VIP: Bogotá, coffee, Cartagena, and Barú](/colombia/tour/colombia-vip-coffee-cartagena-baru-10-days/) | Specific hotels and an island stay |

The table highlights the differences between these particular itineraries. Their included services, accommodation categories, and rates vary.

## A short trip: 5 or 7 days

The [five-day “From the Andes to the Caribbean” tour](/colombia/tour/colombia-essential-5-days/) connects two cities. Bogotá includes the historic center, museums, and the Monserrate viewpoint. A separate outing takes you to [Lake Guatavita](/colombia/place/lake-guatavita/) and the underground Salt Cathedral in [Zipaquirá](/colombia/place/zipaquira/). After a flight to Cartagena, the itinerary continues with walking tours and a day in the [Rosario Islands](/colombia/place/rosario-islands/).

The [seven-day itinerary](/colombia/tour/colombia-highlights-7-days/) adds Medellín, featuring Botero's art, Comuna 13, and an outing to [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/). The Caribbean segment remains part of the trip. This is a good option for travelers who want to see three very different cities and are comfortable with more transfers.

If time is limited, two substantial stops are often better than trying to cover every region of the country. Compare arrival and departure times: 5 calendar days do not always mean 5 full sightseeing days.

## Coffee itineraries: what really sets them apart

In Colombia, coffee can be the central focus of a trip or an addition to visits to historic cities. The [ten-day coffee itinerary](/colombia/tour/colombia-bogota-medellin-cartagena-coffee-10-days/) divides the time between Bogotá and its surroundings, Medellín, and Cartagena. Discovering coffee production is part of a broader cultural itinerary.

The [11-day tour](/colombia/tour/colombia-complete-11-days/) specifically visits [Salento](/colombia/place/salento/), the [Cocora Valley](/colombia/place/cocora-valley/), and [El Ocaso coffee farm](/colombia/place/el-ocaso-coffee-farm/). Cartagena, 3 nights on San Andrés, and Medellín follow. This sequence allows more time in the coffee region and on the island but requires several flights.

If production and tasting matter more than the number of cities, explore our [coffee tours in Colombia](/interests/coffee-tours/tours/colombia/). Within this collection, compare itineraries with a substantial farm visit against those that spend less time on coffee. A tasting, a walk through the plantation, and learning how beans are processed are distinct experiences.

## Caño Cristales: a journey centered on a natural phenomenon

The [eight-day route to the colorful river](/colombia/tour/colombia-cano-cristales-8-days/) is structured differently from standard tours of the main cities. After Bogotá, the main focus shifts to [La Macarena](/colombia/place/la-macarena/). The trip includes separate outings to the river and travel by boat, off-road vehicle, and on foot.

The vivid colors of Caño Cristales are linked to the aquatic plant *Macarenia clavigera*. Colombia's official tourism portal describes the most striking colors as occurring **from May to November**. Access to particular trails depends on local regulations, water levels, and trail conditions. Choose a suitable season first, then check which excursions are available and plan the other days around them.

La Macarena is difficult to add between the coffee region and Cartagena without an extra transport leg. If the colorful river is your main goal, choose an itinerary that genuinely sets aside time for nature excursions. For other options, see [nature-focused tours of Colombia](/interests/wildlife/tours/colombia/).

## Beaches, islands, and the length of your stay

A coastal segment does not always mean staying by the sea. On a short itinerary, the [Rosario Islands](/colombia/place/rosario-islands/) may be a day trip from Cartagena. [Barú Island](/colombia/place/baru-island/) can also be a separate overnight stop. The [VIP Colombia itinerary](/colombia/tour/colombia-vip-coffee-cartagena-baru-10-days/) explicitly names hotels in Bogotá, Pereira, Cartagena, and Barú, including Four Seasons Casa Medina and Las Islas. Those details belong to that specific tour, not to every VIP trip.

The [11-day “Many Faces of Colombia” tour](/colombia/tour/colombia-complete-11-days/) includes 3 nights on San Andrés. That offers a very different experience from a one-day boat excursion.

Before booking, check four practical details: how many nights you actually spend by the sea, how transfers are arranged, whether the beach is a full day of leisure, and which activities are included. Browse the full collection of [beach holidays in Colombia](/interests/beach-holidays/tours/colombia/).

## What to compare before booking

Tour prices vary for reasons other than duration. Current programs offer SGL, DBL, and TRP accommodation arrangements, different hotel categories, and private or mixed formats. Some trips list a minimum price per person, while others publish the scope of their offer without one directly comparable price. A tour's price or level of service should not be applied to a different itinerary.

- **Rate conditions.** Check which accommodation type, group size, and currency a quoted amount refers to.
- **Flights and transfers.** Check domestic flights, boats, baggage allowances, and transportation to natural attractions.
- **Excursions.** See which days already include guides, admission tickets, and activities, and which are offered separately.
- **Physical demands and pace.** Cultural walks, hikes in natural areas, and several flights within a week create very different travel experiences.

Read more about the country in our [Colombia travel guide](/colombia/), and compare further itineraries in the [full travel catalog](/tours/).

## Frequently asked questions about choosing a tour

### Is 5, 7, or 11 days better for a first trip?

Five days work well for Bogotá and Cartagena. The seven-day itinerary adds Medellín. The 11-day program devotes more time to the coffee region and island relaxation. The key is to choose your preferred balance of cities, nature, and sea, rather than the longest possible list of attractions.

### Can I travel to Colombia specifically for coffee?

Yes. The [10-day coffee tour](/colombia/tour/colombia-bogota-medellin-cartagena-coffee-10-days/) combines a farm visit with major cities, while the [11-day route](/colombia/tour/colombia-complete-11-days/) includes Salento, Cocora, and El Ocaso farm. Compare how many days each trip actually dedicates to coffee.

### Can Caño Cristales be visited at any time of year?

No. The river's colors are seasonal, and access depends on visitor regulations and weather conditions. For this journey, choose the [specialist itinerary](/colombia/tour/colombia-cano-cristales-8-days/) rather than counting on an impromptu excursion between cities.

### Do the Rosario Islands and Barú offer the same kind of beach holiday?

No. The Rosario Islands may be the destination of a day trip by boat, while some Barú itineraries include a stay by the sea. Compare the number of nights and the specific services.

### Is a Russian-speaking guide included in every tour?

There is no single language policy covering the entire catalog. The guiding language and included services are specified in each individual tour description.

kind: tour

buttonLabel: "Explore the 'Colombia Metropolitan' tour"
lead: >-
  “Colombia Metropolitan” is a six-day trip featuring Bogotá and Medellín. In the capital, you will discover La Candelaria, the Gold Museum, Monserrate, and an outing to the Salt Cathedral of Zipaquirá. Medellín reveals another side of the country through Botero's art, Comuna 13, modern neighborhoods, and a trip to Guatapé and the Piedra del Peñol rock. It is ideal for travelers interested in cities, history, and public art.
---

## “Colombia Metropolitan”: two cities, two sides of Colombia

Instead of trying to cover several natural and coastal regions at once, this tour focuses on **Bogotá and Medellín**. In 6 days and 5 nights, you will see historic neighborhoods, museum collections, contemporary street art, urban parks, and the scenic surroundings of Medellín.

The first 3 nights are planned in [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/), followed by 2 nights in [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/). A domestic flight connects the cities. Choose this format if you want to understand how life differs between two major Colombian urban centers and beaches and coffee plantations are not your principal goals.

## Bogotá: cultural history in a high-altitude city

In Bogotá, the itinerary brings together the La Candelaria neighborhood, the Gold Museum, Fernando Botero's artworks, Bolívar Square, and an ascent to Monserrate. These landmarks illuminate different periods, from pre-Columbian cultures to colonial architecture and modern art.

A separate day is devoted to the Salt Cathedral in [Zipaquirá](/colombia/place/zipaquira/), built inside a salt mine. We have allocated approximately 5 hours to the trip, including travel and the visit. The city sightseeing tour of Bogotá is estimated at around 6 hours.

The Gold Museum is closed on Mondays. Casa de la Moneda and Donación Botero follow a different schedule, with Tuesday listed as their closing day. Consider these restrictions when choosing your departure date so you do not have to shorten your planned exploration of the capital.

## Medellín: Botero, Comuna 13, and new urban spaces

After the flight to Medellín, a comprehensive sightseeing tour is planned. It takes in San Antonio Park, San Ignacio Square, Avenida La Playa, and the Sculpture Park featuring Botero's works. The route then introduces the Poblado neighborhood, Parque de los Deseos, and other city landmarks.

The **Comuna 13 graffiti tour** is a particular highlight: a walk through the neighborhood, stories of its history and local artists, and a visit to the famous outdoor escalators. This is not a gallery visit; the cultural experience is rooted in the urban environment and the life of the neighborhood itself.

The sightseeing program in Medellín takes about 7 hours and falls on the same day as the flight from Bogotá. The schedule calls for careful flight selection and enough time to reach the city from the airport. If you would prefer a gentler pace, discuss the order of visits in advance.

## Why a city-focused tour includes Guatapé

The following day is spent outside Medellín. The trip visits [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/), Piedra del Peñol, and the Peñol–Guatapé reservoir. It includes a walk through the town with its painted facades and a ride by motorcycle taxi. The excursion lasts approximately 8 hours.

**Climbing the rock and taking a boat trip on the reservoir are not included in the price.** They should not be regarded as mandatory parts of the paid itinerary. If you want to add them, their availability and terms need to be checked separately. The trip to Guatapé itself, transportation, and a typical restaurant lunch are included in the basic tour.

## How excursions and expenses are allocated

| Item | In the itinerary |
|---|---|
| Accommodation | 3 nights in Bogotá, 2 in Medellín |
| Meals | Daily breakfasts |
| Transfers | Airport – hotel – airport |
| Domestic flight | Paid separately |
| Guatapé | Trip and lunch included |
| Rock climb | Additional charge |

The price includes city sightseeing tours in both destinations, Monserrate, Zipaquirá, the Comuna 13 graffiti tour, and the Guatapé excursion with lunch. Private transportation and an English-speaking guide are provided on the relevant excursion days. Air tickets, personal expenses, and optional activities are paid separately.

Museum opening schedules are especially important for the first full sightseeing day in Bogotá, while arrival time matters on the day of the flight to Medellín. Another practical point: the reservoir excursion takes place outside the city, so the actual time spent exploring Medellín is less than the total length of the stay suggests.

## How it differs from coffee and Caribbean itineraries

[“Colombia Coffee”](/colombia/tour/colombia-coffee/) also lasts 6 days, but its second half visits [Pereira](/colombia/place/pereira/), a coffee farm, and the [Cocora Valley](/colombia/place/cocora-valley/). This option suits travelers who prioritize plantations and Andean nature.

[“Colombia Live”](/colombia/tour/colombia-live/) is considerably longer and includes the coast, [Tayrona](/colombia/place/tayrona-national-park/), and [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/). “Metropolitan” stands out for its concentration on urban history, museums, architecture, and street art. Other city combinations are available in the [Colombia tours catalog](/colombia/tour/).

## Frequently asked questions about “Colombia Metropolitan”

### Is the Bogotá–Medellín flight included?

No. Domestic and international air tickets are explicitly listed among the services excluded from the tour price.

### Is the climb up Piedra del Peñol included?

No. The excursion to the Guatapé area is included, but the rock climb and the reservoir boat trip are paid for separately.

### Can I see Medellín without longer excursions outside the city?

The standard itinerary includes a separate sightseeing day outside the city, in Guatapé. Changes to the program and the option to skip that trip are best discussed when arranging a customized itinerary.

### Does the tour include coffee plantations?

No, “Colombia Metropolitan” does not include a visit to a coffee farm. If this is your goal, choose an [itinerary with a coffee farm](/colombia/tour/colombia-coffee/) instead.

targetPath: /colombia/tour/santa-marta-lost-city-2023/
kind: tour
status: approved
locale: en
buttonLabel: "Learn more about the Lost City trek"
lead: >-
  A journey to the Lost City in the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta takes 7 days, several of them spent trekking through humid tropical forest. After the ascent to the ancient stone terraces of the Tairona people, the trip continues with relaxation on the Caribbean coast. Learn about the physical demands, overnight conditions, protected-area rules, and how to prepare for this route.
---

## Trekking to the Lost City: what to expect over 7 days

The main destination of this journey is the [Lost City of Teyuna](/colombia/place/ciudad-perdida/), an archaeological site of the Tairona culture in the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta mountains. Reaching its stone terraces and stairways requires a multi-day hike through jungle and river valleys. The trip therefore demands time for the route itself, physical preparation, and a willingness to stay in simple accommodation.

The tour begins in [Santa Marta](/colombia/place/santa-marta/) with a city excursion, before heading into the mountains and returning to the coast. The schedule covers 7 days and 6 nights: 1 night in Santa Marta, 3 nights in the Lost City area, and 2 nights near [Tayrona National Park](/colombia/place/tayrona-national-park/). This combination works for travelers who enjoy archaeology, trekking, and a short rest after physical exertion.

**This is an active expedition segment, not a bus excursion to the ruins.** Expect steep ascents, slippery sections after rain, river crossings, and stone steps. Colombia's Institute of Anthropology and History, ICANH, explicitly states that Teyuna can only be reached on foot and requires a certified guide.

## The route through the mountains

| Day | Hiking section |
|---|---|
| 2 | El Mamey to the first camp, 7.6 km |
| 3 | Via Mutanzhi to camp, 14 km |
| 4 | Teyuna and the return trail, 9 km |
| 5 | Descent to El Mamey, approximately 7 km |

These distances reflect the Ada Tours itinerary. They are estimates for this particular route, not a standard that applies to every trip to Teyuna. Each section's duration depends on trail conditions, weather, and the group's pace.

On day two, the journey from Santa Marta begins by car and continues by off-road pickup through [El Mamey](/colombia/place/el-mamey/). After lunch, the group starts walking to [Cabaña de Adán](/colombia/place/cabana-de-adan/), where the night is spent in a hammock. On day three, the trail passes through [Mutanzhi](/colombia/place/mutanzhi/), the territory of a local community, and climbs toward the next camp. The itinerary allocates about 7 hours of walking to this day.

On day four, the group sets out before sunrise. A staircase leading to the stone terraces begins just before the archaeological complex. After exploring the site, the group follows mountain trails back to an overnight camp. Day five is dedicated to a long descent and a return to the sea. The full tour program above gives the exact camp names and sequence of stops; it is worth reading in full before planning your trip.

## Why Teyuna is different from an ordinary archaeological museum

Teyuna is a surviving part of a pre-Hispanic Tairona settlement. Its slopes contain stone terraces, circular platforms, stairways, and water channels. These structures made it possible to build homes and communal spaces on challenging terrain. Much of the experience comes from the setting itself: the site cannot be separated from the forest, the mountains, or the trail leading to it.

The Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta is still home to Indigenous communities. Visiting requires respect for the people and their sacred places. Ask permission before photographing residents, homes, or ceremonies, and follow the instructions of the guide and local authorities. If a specific itinerary mentions meeting members of a local community, the format should be agreed upon with the host community, without expecting a staged performance for visitors.

## How to assess the physical challenge

The longest stated day's trek covers approximately 14 km. Distance alone does not determine the difficulty, however: humidity, heat, ascent and descent, slippery rocks, and stairways all matter. Even someone accustomed to long city walks will benefit from preparing for several consecutive days of hiking with a backpack.

Before traveling, assess your ability to walk for long periods in a hot, humid climate. Sensible preparation includes several practice hikes over uneven ground, breaking in your footwear, and deciding how much to carry in your daypack. If you have medical conditions or mobility limitations, discuss the hike with your doctor and the organizer. ICANH specifically notes that the trail has no facilities for visitors with reduced mobility.

Bring quick-drying clothing, reliable grippy footwear, rain protection, a hat, sunscreen, insect repellent, a personal first-aid kit, and waterproof bags for your belongings. Mobile service is unavailable on parts of the route, so tell loved ones in advance when you expect to return and how long you may be out of contact.

## Overnight stays and meals: realistic expectations

The mountain portion of this tour includes overnight stays at camps. Hammocks are provided for sleeping, and beds or tents may also be available at one stage. Conditions are markedly different from a hotel in Santa Marta and from the seaside accommodation after the trek.

Meals along the trekking route are included, but not every meal on the coast is covered. After the return from the mountains, accommodation is planned at Ecohabs Resort; lunch and dinner on day six are paid for separately. Personal expenses, tips, air tickets, and services beyond those listed are also excluded. When comparing itineraries, check the exact number of camp nights, which meals are included, and any extra costs.

## The coast after the trek: why it is part of the trip

Day five ends with a return to the Caribbean coast, and day six gives you time to relax by the sea. This is a purposeful end to the hike: after early starts and long walks, you can swap mountain trails for the beach. A transfer to Santa Marta airport is scheduled for day seven.

[Tayrona National Park](/colombia/place/tayrona-national-park/) sometimes restricts access to particular sectors, both seasonally and at other times. Available entrances and trails change according to park administration decisions, so the beach segment must be checked against the rules in effect for your travel dates. Included activities and optional extras are different: a walk or horseback ride to neighboring beaches is listed as a separately charged option.

## When to plan the trek

The Sierra Nevada has rainy and comparatively drier periods, although rain is possible in different months. During the wet season, river levels and trail conditions are especially important for safety. A date on the calendar alone cannot guarantee access to every section of the route.

Besides weather, **official closure periods for Teyuna** must be checked. Closures may be established to help nature recover and to allow Indigenous communities to hold spiritual ceremonies. Before confirming the trip, we will help check your dates against visitor rules and the availability of the confirmed route. The historical year in this page's address is not itself the date of a future departure.

## Frequently asked questions about the Lost City

### Can I visit Teyuna without a multi-day hike?

No. There is no vehicle access directly to the archaeological complex. Under ICANH rules, visitors reach the site on trails with a certified guide. This is the main criterion when choosing the trip: duration and physical effort are integral parts of the experience.

### How many days of the tour are spent hiking?

On Ada Tours' seven-day itinerary, the main treks take place from day two through day five. Day one is dedicated to Santa Marta, while the final 2 days include the coast and departure.

### Do I need experience in difficult mountain climbs?

Mountaineering skills are not listed as a requirement, but good physical fitness is necessary. What matters most is being ready for several successive days of long walks, humid heat, changes in elevation, and simple overnight accommodation.

### Are lunches and dinners after the trek included?

Meals along the mountain route are included. Some meals during the beach segment cost extra: for example, the itinerary expressly excludes lunch and dinner on day six. Check the full list of services for your particular departure.

### Can I count on mobile phone coverage in the forest?

No. ICANH warns that there is no mobile signal along the route in the Teyuna area. Arrange in advance to contact family and friends after returning to Santa Marta.

targetPath: /colombia/tour/viva-colombia/
kind: tour
status: approved
locale: en
buttonLabel: "Explore the 'Viva Colombia' journey"
lead: >-
  “Viva Colombia” brings together Bogotá, Medellín, the coffee valleys, and Cartagena over 10 days. The pace is active, with several domestic flights, walks through high-altitude cities, and a dedicated day on a coffee plantation. The itinerary is ideal for travelers who want to discover Colombia's cities, coffee country, and Cartagena without a long beach holiday.
---

## “Viva Colombia”: who will enjoy this 10-day journey?

This itinerary is designed for travelers who want to experience different parts of Colombia in a single trip. It covers pre-Columbian history, museums, Andean cities, mountain scenery, coffee cultivation, and the architecture of the Caribbean coast. Almost every day, however, is filled with sightseeing or travel between regions. If your main goal is to spend several free days by the sea, consider the [14-day journey including the Rosario Islands](/colombia/tour/colombia-2024/).

The main advantage of the ten-day itinerary is that you experience four distinct regions of Colombia in sequence. The trip begins in [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/) with history and high-altitude surroundings. [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/) places more emphasis on contemporary urban culture. In the coffee region, exploring nature leads into a hands-on farm visit. [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/) introduces the historic Caribbean coast.

## How the days and transfers are arranged

| Stage | Main highlights |
|---|---|
| Days 1–3 | Bogotá, museums, Guatavita, Zipaquirá |
| Days 4–5 | Medellín, Guatapé, urban culture |
| Days 6–7 | Cocora, Salento, coffee hacienda |
| Days 8–10 | Cartagena, fortifications, departure |

Day two already includes a walk through the capital's historic center, the Gold Museum, a trip up Monserrate, and the Botero Museum. The following day, the route leaves the city for [Lake Guatavita](/colombia/place/lake-guatavita/), associated with the legend of El Dorado, and [Zipaquirá](/colombia/place/zipaquira/) with its underground Salt Cathedral. These are 2 separate sightseeing days, not a single short stop in Bogotá.

Next come a flight to Medellín and a trip to [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/). The contrast is striking: after the capital's museums, the route leads to a small town with brightly painted houses and the El Peñón de Guatapé monolith. The following day focuses on Medellín itself: Botero Square, the Museum of Antioquia, Comuna 13, and other neighborhoods. Comfortable footwear is useful for the longer walks during this part of the trip.

## The coffee region: nature and work on a plantation

After a flight to [Pereira](/colombia/place/pereira/), the journey continues through the [Cocora Valley](/colombia/place/cocora-valley/), home to towering wax palms, and [Salento](/colombia/place/salento/) with its traditional architecture. A separate day is reserved for visiting [Hacienda Venecia](/colombia/place/hacienda-venecia/). This is an important distinguishing feature of “Viva Colombia”: the coffee segment combines a walk through Andean scenery with a dedicated activity at a working farm.

At the hacienda, the coffee experience begins with growing and harvesting beans. The program explains cleaning and sorting methods, offers opportunities to take part in certain stages, and includes a workshop on preparing coffee. You will learn about agriculture and why processing and brewing methods influence flavor. Travelers choosing a trip primarily for coffee may also want to explore our [coffee tours](/interests/coffee-tours/).

Colombia's Coffee Cultural Landscape is inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List. Its value extends beyond the harvest: small farms, mountainous terrain, and historic settlements form a distinctive rural culture. That is why the coffee region is worth exploring even for someone who rarely drinks coffee.

## Cartagena ends the journey without a separate beach week

On day eight, travelers fly from Pereira to Cartagena. Day nine is devoted to the historic center and its defenses. Stops include the San Felipe de Barajas Fortress, old streets, and the monastery on La Popa hill. A transfer to the airport is scheduled for the morning of day ten.

[Cartagena's fortifications and monuments](/colombia/place/cartagena/) are inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List. Their location reflects the city's importance as a major Caribbean port and the need to defend its harbor. This final stop completes the historical arc of the journey, from pre-Columbian cultures in Bogotá to the colonial period on the coast.

It is important to interpret “Caribbean” in the region's name correctly. On this tour, Cartagena is primarily a city and sightseeing stop. A multi-day stay on the beaches of the [Rosario Islands](/colombia/place/rosario-islands/) is not part of “Viva Colombia.”

## What to consider when planning

The route involves 3 domestic flights: Bogotá–Medellín, Medellín–Pereira, and Pereira–Cartagena. These flights are included in the tour price. International flights, optional excursions, drinks, and excess-baggage charges are listed separately. Before booking your international tickets, compare your arrival time with the first day of the program and check baggage allowances on domestic flights.

Travelers are at considerable altitude after arriving in Bogotá and during the outing to Guatavita. Allow time for sleep and gradual adjustment to physical activity over the first few days. Pack clothing for cooler mountain regions, sun protection, and lighter clothing for warmer Cartagena. Comfortable shoes are useful throughout a trip that combines city walks, mountain surroundings, and a farm visit.

If free evenings are important, pay attention to how sightseeing time is distributed. Four geographic stages in 10 days offer great variety but leave less room for leisurely relaxation. We can discuss the order of transfers and the arrangements for your particular departure while preserving the substantive itinerary.

## Frequently asked questions about “Viva Colombia”

### Is this itinerary suitable for a first trip to Colombia?

Yes, if you want to experience the country's main contrasts on one journey and are comfortable with a busy schedule. The capital, Medellín, coffee country, and Cartagena are all included. A gentler pace and island relaxation feature in another [14-day tour of Colombia](/colombia/tour/colombia-2024/).

### Can I visit a coffee plantation, rather than just buy coffee?

Yes. Day seven is dedicated to Hacienda Venecia, with explanations of coffee growing, processing, and preparation. The previous day includes Cocora and Salento, so the coffee region takes up more than a brief stop.

### Are domestic flights included?

The current “Viva Colombia” itinerary specifically includes the Bogotá–Medellín, Medellín–Pereira, and Pereira–Cartagena flights. International tickets and excess baggage are not included. Other tours may have different conditions.

### Are there free days by the Caribbean Sea?

There are no dedicated beach days on this itinerary: day eight involves a flight, day nine a Cartagena excursion, and day ten departure. For a longer seaside stay, consider the [itinerary featuring the Rosario Islands](/colombia/tour/colombia-2024/).

### How much will the weather vary during the trip?

The journey begins in high-altitude Bogotá, crosses green Andean regions, and finishes on the Caribbean coast. A single set of clothes is therefore impractical for all 10 days: prepare for cool mountain conditions as well as warm weather by the sea.

## Excursion to Villa de Leyva: a colonial town and traces of an ancient sea

Villa de Leyva lies in Colombia's Boyacá department. Its white houses with tiled roofs, stone streets, and spacious central square have preserved the appearance of a colonial town. Around the square are churches, historic houses, museums, small restaurants, and arcaded courtyards.

Ada Tours offers a dedicated [“Villa de Leyva” excursion](/colombia/villa-de-leyva/villa-de-leyva-tour/) lasting **12 hours**. The route combines a walk through the historic center, regional history, the Boyacá Bridge, and paleontology. It appeals to travelers eager to discover Colombia beyond its major cities and explore several chapters of the country's past.

## What to see on the excursion

Villa de Leyva's defining landmark is the large cobblestoned Plaza Mayor. White facades, balconies, and church buildings surround it. The square offers an excellent view of the proportions typical of Spanish colonial architecture. Its vast open stone surface is particularly impressive, with the surrounding mountains reminding visitors that the town stands in the Andean highlands.

During your walk, look for arches, inner courtyards, stone doorways, and the local street layout. Colombia's official tourism portal highlights the Church of Nuestra Señora del Rosario and numerous examples of colonial architecture.

The itinerary includes the **historic Boyacá Bridge**. This site is associated with Colombia's struggle for independence. Because it is a separate landmark elsewhere in the region, check in advance how much time is allocated to this particular stop.

## Why fossils are part of the story

The town and its surroundings are known for paleontological discoveries. Many millions of years ago, marine basins covered parts of what are now the Andes, and the local rocks still contain remains of ancient animals. The Fossil Museum, paleontological collections, and discoveries of marine reptiles are important parts of Villa de Leyva's visitor appeal.

The [Ada Tours excursion](/colombia/villa-de-leyva/villa-de-leyva-tour/) introduces fossils and the region's paleontological heritage. However, its terms do not specify a particular museum, its opening hours, or the price of separate admission. If your priority is to study a collection in depth or see a particular famous find, arrange the museum visit separately.

For more on the town itself, its architecture, and walks, visit the [Villa de Leyva destination page](/colombia/place/villa-de-leyva/). This catalog will help you choose an excursion.

## How to prepare for the walk

Cobblestoned streets and the open square call for comfortable shoes. In the Andes, sun, cloud cover, and temperatures can change quickly, so bring water, sun protection, and a light warm layer. White facades, arcades, and local stone paving photograph particularly well, but leave time for an unhurried stroll in addition to taking pictures.
